conventions.confidence: high = breed standard / peer-reviewed / vet association and consistent across sources; medium = single reputable source or sources disagree a little; low = secondary source, strong disagreement, or derived/proposal
conventions.unsourced: Anything with source_id null is marked 'UNSOURCED — proposal' and must not be shown to parents/children as fact.
conventions.quotes: Quotes are as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-05; spot-check against the URL before import.
conventions.game_time: 1 real week = 1 month of dog age (REALISM_SPEC §2).
conventions.decision: "potrdil David 2026-10-05: …" = the game value David confirmed (DECISIONS 2026-10-05). It is a product decision, NOT literature: source_id stays the underlying evidence and is null where the literature gives no number.

logistic_model.description: Logistic curve y = a / (1 + exp(-(x - x0)/b)), x in weeks. Shape parameters = arithmetic mean of the four 'medium' breeds in S9 (Fox Terrier, Teckel, Basset Hound, Beagle); a = adult weight of the target dog.
logistic_model.check: Implied time to 99 percent adult weight = x0 + b*ln(99) = 57.4 weeks, consistent with S9 T99 of 52-58 weeks for the medium breeds.
logistic_model.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. Neither Border Collie nor mixed breeds were in S9 (21 dogs). Applying the medium-breed shape to them is an assumption. Interpretation of 1/b as % per week is ours; it is consistent with the reported T99. Model is not valid near birth.

percent_of_adult_weight_by_month.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. Computed from logistic_model (S9 medium-breed shape).

akc.quote: Approximate weight of dogs and bitches in working condition: dogs 65 to 80 pounds; bitches 55 to 70 pounds.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value, not breed-specific. Labrador AKC males 65–80 lb are 'Large'; bitches 55–70 lb straddle Medium (24–59 lb: 12–15 months) and Large. Salt (S8): 'larger breeds requiring up to 24 months to reach adult body weight'. Quote is a table row on the page (Large (59–99 pounds) | 15–18 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. Not derived: the existing logistic shape (general_by_size.growth.logistic_model) is a MEDIUM-breed curve (≈99 % at 57 weeks) and would contradict the large-breed 15–18 months (S10). A large-breed curve needs a source (S9 has no large breed; Salt 2017 raw data not downloadable). Open question for David.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (Sci Rep), corrected Figure 3 legend (author correction, same document as S16, read from the LJMU repository copy because PMC was not reachable). The Dogs Trust summary page (S15) does not list the Labrador. Conflicts with S55 (12.0 y).

median_uk_vetcompass_2018.quote: The median longevity of Labrador retrievers overall was 12.0 years (IQR 9.9–13.8, range 0.0–16.0).
median_uk_vetcompass_2018.notes: McGreevy, Wilson, …, O'Neill (2018) — VetCompass, 33,320 Labradors under care in 2013; longevity from the deaths in a random sample. Colour effect: 'The median longevity of non-chocolate coloured dogs (n = 139, 12.1 years…' vs '…chocolate coloured animals (n = 34, 10.7 years…' (S55; press summary S56).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25% of lifespan (S11) × median 13.1 y (S54) → 0.75 × 13.1 = 9.8 y = 118 months (same as Border Collie). With the VetCompass median 12.0 y (S55): 0.75 × 12.0 = 9.0 y = 108 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y (S14).

health._note: Parent-facing background only. Brachycephaly is the breed's defining welfare issue and every source on the breed raises it; recorded factually with sources, no invented percentages. Percentages below come from clinic records or a self-selected testing scheme — each carries its context; do not show any of them to children. Breathing/heat are proposed as a gentle game mechanic (proposed_game_parameters.french_bulldog.heat_breathing_mechanic), not as statistics.

brachycephaly_boas.value: flat-faced (brachycephalic) breed; at risk of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) — narrow nostrils, excess soft tissue, noisy/laboured breathing
brachycephaly_boas.quote: The soft tissue in the nose and throat of some brachycephalic dogs may be excessive for the airways
brachycephaly_boas.notes: RKC breed page (S78) also: 'Some dogs may also have narrow nostrils making it even more difficult to breathe.'; 'dogs with a very flat face and short muzzle have a higher risk of developing certain health issues'; 'Not all flat-faced dogs will have the health issues described'. PDSA (S81): 'Frenchies are a flat-faced breed, which can often cause breathing problems.'; BOAS 'can cause severe breathing problems and is caused by their shorter faces.' Woodgreen (S82): 'Unfortunately, Frenchies are prone to several health conditions including breathing problems'. Cambridge (S90): BOAS is 'a progressive disorder that can impair a dog's ability to exercise, play, eat and sleep'. Standards: FCI (S76) 'The slope of the nostrils as well as the upturned nose must, however, allow normal nasal breathing.' — disqualifying faults 'Respiratory distress.' and 'Completely closed nostrils.'; RKC (S79) 'Dogs showing respiratory distress or making excessive respiratory noise unacceptable.'

boas_odds_vs_other_dogs.unit: odds ratio vs non-French Bulldogs (UK primary care, 2016)
boas_odds_vs_other_dogs.notes: O'Neill et al. 2021 (S84), 2,781 French Bulldogs vs 21,850 other dogs: BOAS OR 30.89; stenotic nares '(OR 42.14; 95 % CI 18.50 to 95.99; p < 0.001)'; also aural discharge OR 14.40, skin fold dermatitis OR 11.18, dystocia OR 9.13. Increased odds for '20/43 (46.5 %) disorders', reduced for '11/43 (25.6 %)'. Conclusion: 'the health of French Bulldogs has diverged substantially from, and may be lower than,' [the rest of the dog population — completion paraphrased]; 'Many of these predispositions are closely associated with the conformational extremes that define the French Bulldog breed.' Odds ratios = relative risk of a vet recording the diagnosis, NOT the share of Frenchies affected.

boas_diagnosed_prevalence_2013.unit: % of French Bulldogs with a recorded BOAS diagnosis in one year (2013)
boas_diagnosed_prevalence_2013.notes: O'Neill et al. 2018 (S83), 2,228 French Bulldogs, median age 1.3 y. A one-year recorded-diagnosis rate in a very young population — the paper notes older dogs were significantly more likely to have a BOAS diagnosis (paraphrase), so it understates lifetime risk. Do NOT present as 'only 2.4 % are affected'.

rfg_grades_2024.unit: % of French Bulldogs graded in the RKC/Cambridge Respiratory Function Grading scheme (cumulative to 31/12/2024)
rfg_grades_2024.notes: Row of the RKC annual RFG report 2024 (S89); column headers were garbled and matched to Grade 0–3 by position by the tool (counts sum to 1,831; 301 tested in 2024). Self-selected population (mostly dogs of health-testing breeders) — NOT representative of pet Frenchies. Scheme (S90): grade 0–3 after an exercise tolerance test; 'dogs graded as three will show severe respiratory signs of BOAS'; 'The scheme issues guidance that dogs graded three should not be bred from.' Grade definitions 0–2 not returned.

heat_stroke.value: higher risk of heat-related illness; brachycephalic dogs OR 2.10 vs mesocephalic; French Bulldog about 6× (odds vs Labrador, press summary)

standard_poodle._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-07, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S118–S123, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). Pages were partly returned as paraphrase — only passages the tool returned in quotation marks are used as quotes. The FCI standard covers four Poodle varieties; this entry is the Standard (large) variety only, which the RKC lists as its own breed 'Poodle (Standard)'. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 (S54) does not name any Poodle in its text / corrected Fig. 3 legend; the Dogs Trust life-expectancy table of the same study (S123) has a single 'Poodle' row (14.0 y) that pools all varieties — not variety-specific, so not used for the Standard (size drives longevity); no VetCompass Standard Poodle median found → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S120). Weight: neither the FCI (S118) nor the RKC (S121) standard gives a weight; PDSA (S122, tier B, 'Poodle' page, size Large) is the only weight range. Woodgreen and AKC pages not found / not attempted.

identity.quote: FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 9 Companion and Toy dogs.

Varieties: Standard, Medium size, Miniature, Toy. FCI PDF (S118): 'FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 9 Companion and Toy dogs.' 'Section 2 Poodle.' 'Without working trial.' 'ORIGIN: France'. The RKC breed page says the Poodle 'originates in Germany, where it was bred as a water retriever' (S120, paraphrase) — FCI country of origin used.

size_class.notes: RKC breed page (S120). PDSA (S122) says 'Size: Large' (key-facts box as returned) — conflict; RKC breed page preferred (runbook §2.2). Height FCI 45–60 cm (S118); PDSA weight 21–35 kg (S122) = PetMD Medium / Large class boundary (S10).

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 21–35 kg (S122) = 46–77 lb: males 66–77 lb (Large class), females 46–70 lb (straddles 'Medium (24–59 pounds): 12–15 months'); the midpoint 28 kg ≈ 62 lb → Large. Alternative: Medium 12–15 months.

mcmillan_poodle_pooled.unit: years (median life expectancy, all Poodle varieties pooled)
mcmillan_poodle_pooled.notes: Dogs Trust table 'LIFE EXPECTANCY FOR 155 BREEDS AND CROSSBRED GROUP' (S123, the McMillan et al. 2024 data — S15 / S54): one 'Poodle' row, no Standard / Miniature / Toy rows. Pools the varieties, so it is not a Standard Poodle value (smaller dogs live longer, S54) — recorded as an alternative only; not exported (would read as the Standard's median).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 12 y (S120; PDSA 12–14 y lower bound agrees, S122) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (no Standard Poodle value — only the pooled 'Poodle' row, S123) → VetCompass median (none found for the Standard) → RKC lower bound. With the pooled 14.0 y: 0.75 × 14 × 12 = 126 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until a variety-specific McMillan / VetCompass value is checked.

dachshund._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-08, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S124–S130, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). This entry is the STANDARD-size Dachshund (FCI variety a 'Standard'; RKC 'Dachshund (Smooth Haired)', one of six UK varieties that 'all share the same breed standard, divided by size and coat', S125); the portrait and the app use the smooth coat. Miniature values are recorded as alternatives only. The FCI standard PDF (148g04-en) could not be read (redirect loop https↔http, 2026-10-10) → identity from the FCI nomenclature page (S124), appearance and weight from the RKC standard (S126). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 names only the 'Miniature Dachshund' (14.0 y, via press S130); no standard-size McMillan / VetCompass median found → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S125). Welfare-concern breed (runbook §3): long-backed, short-legged conformation → intervertebral disc disease (BVA S128, RKC IVDD screening scheme S125, PDSA S127 / S129) → new consider tag `back_spine`. No advice against showing dachshunds in advertising found (BVA S128, excerpts; UFAW not fetchable) → stays in marketing; spot-check S128 before a campaign.

identity.notes: FCI nomenclature page (S124, fields as returned): standard number 148, 'Country of origin: GERMANY', subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance 1/1/1955, official valid standard 5/25/2021. Group 4 has no numbered section; varieties a) Standard, b) Miniature, c) Rabbit Dachshund, each smooth-, long- and wire-haired. RKC breed page (S125): 'Originating in Germany where he is known as the Teckel (badger dog) the Dachshund'.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; never shown in the app as a statistic. Welfare-concern breed: the long, low body shape predisposes to intervertebral disc disease (BVA S128, PDSA S127 / S129); RKC Breed Watch 'Category 2' (S125) and the KC IVDD screening scheme strongly recommended before breeding (S125). The BVA article's risk multiple and onset ages stay out of the app, the export and the audience docs (runbook: no statistics). Colour Watch 'Category 2: Breeds with >2 to 10% registered NBS colours' (S125); the RKC refuses registrations from certain dapple matings because of vision / hearing risks (S125) → the app and portraits never draw dapple.

back_ivdd.quote: Certain breeds such as the Dachshund and French bulldog are prone to IVDD and slipped discs due to the shape of their spine.
back_ivdd.notes: PDSA IVDD page (S129); PDSA breed page (S127): 'Both standard and miniature varieties are affected by back problems.'; RKC (S125): 'Spine screening using the KC intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) screening scheme (supported by Dachshund Health UK)'; BVA (S128): 'tops the list of common health issues' (as returned). Prevention (S129): keep the dog the right weight; avoid 'chasing, jumping or going up and down stairs' (advice given for recovery).

conformation_welfare.quote: always pick health over looks or Insta-appeal
conformation_welfare.notes: BVA news 9 Mar 2020 (S128): vets urge prospective owners to 'be aware of the spinal issues' and 'speak to their vet for tailored advice' (as returned). No BVA advice against showing dachshunds in advertising (S128).

siberian_husky._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-13, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S158–S165, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). The PDSA page (S162) was returned partly as paraphrase with quotes capped at ~120 characters — only passages the tool returned in quotation marks are used as quotes; longer sentences are cut where the tool cut them. Every S162 quote used (energy, children, exercise, escaping, chewing, shedding, grooming, hip dysplasia) was re-checked character for character on a second fetch (2026-10-10, review of PR #161) — all present verbatim, including the page's own typo 'The have heaps of energy'. McMillan et al. 2024 (S54 / S135) names no Siberian Husky in its text or legends; its Supplementary Table 3, the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) and the 'shortest and longest' PDF were not reachable (fetch error 2026-10-10); Teng et al. 2022 (UK life tables) mentions the 'Husky' only in its sample list and probability-of-death sentences, the Husky life table itself (Table 3) was not reachable; no VetCompass Siberian Husky median found — so the lifespan is the RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S160) per the runbook rule. The mixed-breed baseline (1.0) is unranked and treated as 'Average'. The existing scale spends ~0.3 per Coren tier step (Average 1.0 → Above average → Excellent → Brightest ≈ 1.8–2.0, i.e. 3 steps for +0.8–1.0), so one step down = 0.7. No individual variation (like the other pedigree breeds). Mixed breed with ±20 % can be as slow as 0.8 — overlaps with the alternative.

heat_breathing_mechanic.notes: UNSOURCED idea, not built (post-MVP backlog). Must NOT use a weather API (CLAUDE.md scope guard). Sourced facts it rests on: overheat and struggle to breathe quickly in warm weather, walk in cooler morning/evening, know the heatstroke signs (PDSA S81); 'two good walks a day' (Woodgreen S82); OR 2.10 for heat illness in flat-faced dogs (S86); noisy breathing at rest is not normal (RKC standard S79 'excessive respiratory noise unacceptable'). Idea: (1) the daily step goal counts only in ≥ 2 walks — one walk above ~30 min (half the goal; our number) makes the dog 'pant' and pause (child learns: short walks, rests); (2) in the game's summer months (calendar, family timezone — no weather data) midday walks (e.g. 11–16 h, our number) trigger a 'too hot — walk in the morning or evening' hint and a water reminder; (3) a calm 'Did you know?' card: flat faces can make breathing harder, so Frenchies need cool shade, water and gentle walks. No illness, collapse or death shown to the child; no percentages.

marketing.value: in the app: yes; in marketing: yes (not a conformation welfare-concern breed; no veterinary advice against showing the breed in advertising)
marketing.notes: RKC Breed Watch 'Category 2' (S164) lists only 'Too fat' and 'Too thin' — show body condition, not a conformation exaggeration; moderate standard (FCI S158: 'Any appearance of excessive bone or weight should be penalized.'). The only veterinary advice against advertising a breed type is for flat-faced breeds (S92). Marketing never promises health and never shows a Husky as an easy dog for small children (PDSA S162).
marketing.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-10 (pravilo runbooka): in the app yes, in marketing yes (no veterinary advice against advertising the breed)
